consensus: Kinnan is a mana-combo commander, and strong lists are combo decks with a ramp shell rather than ramp decks with a combo. They run an extreme density of nonland mana permanents, double their output with Kinnan's static, and convert a large or infinite pool through a dedicated OUTLET. The nucleus is Kinnan + Basalt Monolith -- two cards, one of them the commander -- for infinite colourless; Basalt Monolith is in 88% of 20,837 EDHREC lists. Kinnan's own {5}{G}{U} ability is a digger, not a kill: with infinite mana it puts every non-Human creature in the library onto the battlefield, and what wins is what it finds. Thrasios, Triton Hero sits in the 99 of 74% of lists (15.4K decks) as the sink that draws the deck. Interaction is free and cheap counterspells held up over the combo turn, not a removal suite.

findings.claim: The mana base is nonland permanents, not lands. EDHREC's average Kinnan deck is 29 creatures, 15 artifacts, 17 instants, 5 sorceries, 5 enchantments, 1 planeswalker and 27 LANDS -- roughly ten under the 36-38 convention, paid for by dorks and rocks Kinnan then doubles. The split in the pilot's collection is clean and it is not 'he owns nothing'. He already owns 12 of the mana pieces these lists run -- Birds of Paradise, Llanowar Elves, Elvish Mystic, Fyndhorn Elves, Elvish Spirit Guide, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Selvala, Heart of the Wilds, Devoted Druid, Axebane Guardian, Scuttlemutt and Drover of the Mighty, the last three of which are named pieces in the Freed from the Real lines. What he owns none of is the ARTIFACT half, and that half contains the deck's single most included card: all 15 cards listed here are absent from the 931-name collection.

Kinnan + Basalt Monolith is the nucleus and is near-universal: Basalt Monolith is in 88% of all 20,837 Kinnan lists (18.3K decks) and 89% of the 1,262 lists EDHREC's Optimized (bracket 4) filter returns. Tap for {C}{C}{C}, Kinnan adds a fourth, pay {3} to untap -- net +1 per iteration, and one of the two cards is in the command zone.

Infinite mana is converted by a dedicated OUTLET, not by Kinnan's activated ability alone. Drake Sasser writes that infinite mana is 'spent on the outlets that seal the game such Thrasios, Triton Hero, Walking Ballista, and Finale of Devastation'. Kinnan's {5}{G}{U} digs five and puts a non-Human creature into play, so with infinite mana it assembles every non-Human creature in the library -- which is a board, and needs Craterhoof Behemoth or an attack step to be a kill. Thrasios is the clean answer: infinite activations draw the deck, and Thrasios is a Merfolk Wizard, so Kinnan can fetch it.

There is a second infinite engine that does NOT need Kinnan on the battlefield: Hullbreaker Horror or Tidespout Tyrant plus two net-positive mana artifacts loops by bouncing and recasting them, generating infinite mana and infinite storm. Hullbreaker Horror is in 81% of lists (16.8K decks), Tidespout Tyrant 50% (10.3K). This is the redundancy that keeps the deck from being one two-mana 2/2 wide.

Bracket 4 imposes NO card restrictions, so a bracket-4 Kinnan is not a defanged Kinnan. WotC's brackets beta gives Bracket 4 (Optimized) and Bracket 5 (cEDH) the identical rule -- 'There are no restrictions (other than the banned list)' -- while Bracket 3 (Upgraded) is the one that reads 'Up to three cards from the Game Changers list. No intentional early-game two-card infinite combos.' The empirical check agrees: in EDHREC's Optimized filter (1,262 decks) Basalt Monolith is still 89% and Pemmin's Aura 37%. Bracket-4 players do not cut the infinites; what separates 4 from 5 is metagame tuning, per Jeff Girten -- 'cEDH commanders are the cream of the crop AND their decklists are built to combat an existing meta'.

A Kinnan built WITHOUT the infinites is a different deck, and the sources describe it as a big-creature ramp deck rather than a combo deck. A.L. Walser's mid-power build runs 33 lands, states it has 'no infinite combos' intentionally, and wins by deploying Koma, Cosmos Serpent / Vorinclex / Craterhoof Behemoth on turn 3-4 off doubled dork mana, with Kinnan + Seedborn Muse + Training Grounds or Biomancer's Familiar as a repeatable tutor engine and a Kogla, the Titan Ape + Eternal Witness loop for grindy games. That deck is real, but it is a fair deck that a bracket-4 pod can interact with; it is not what the 88% Basalt Monolith figure describes.

Strong lists solve interaction with CHEAP AND FREE COUNTERSPELLS, not with spot removal. TheGamer's guide names the package as free counters -- Force of Will, Fierce Guardianship, Pact of Negation -- backed by conditional one-manners; EDHREC's fleet-wide figures put Mental Misstep at 55% (11.4K decks), Mindbreak Trap 52% (10.8K) and Veil of Summer 42% (8.66K), and the Optimized filter's top instants are Mana Drain 41%, Chord of Calling 40% and Flusterstorm 39%. The stated premise is that the deck is tapped out on its combo turn, so the answers that matter cost zero or one mana. None of the sources I fetched builds Kinnan's interaction out of spot removal. Whether that transfers to a bracket-4 pod is a question for diagnose mode, not something recon can settle.

THE DATA QUESTION, SETTLED. The repo's bracket-1 tag on the three-card Freed from the Real lines is inherited verbatim from upstream, not a repo bug. Commander Spellbook's own page for Kinnan + Basalt Monolith reads 'Ruthless (Bracket 4+)', while its page for Kinnan + Bloom Tender + Freed from the Real reads 'Exhibition (Bracket 1+)' and says the rating was 'estimated'. Spellbook's bracket field is a community-estimated FLOOR ('1+', '4+'), and for the three-card lines the estimate has evidently defaulted low. The lines themselves are standard, not fringe: EDHREC counts Kinnan + Birds of Paradise + Freed from the Real in 15,096 decks and Kinnan + Bloom Tender + Freed from the Real in 11,515. Do not read a Spellbook bracket as a power rating.

The deck's tutoring is its named structural weakness, because Simic has none of the good ones. Sasser calls the Simic package 'steep downgrades' (Moonsilver Key, Transmute Artifact against Demonic Tutor) and notes Kinnan is locked out of Dockside Extortionist and Underworld Breach. What lists run instead is creature-tutoring that also finds the mana: Green Sun's Zenith is in 51% of lists (10.7K decks), Fabricate 46%, Moonsilver Key 50%, Transmute Artifact 40%, Nature's Rhythm 51%.

Speed, as ASSERTED by the sources. No source I fetched gives a measured win-turn distribution. Felipe Torres writes a budget Kinnan 'can go infinite as soon as on turn 3'; TheGamer's guide claims combo victories 'as early as turn one'; A.L. Walser's mid-power build describes turn 3-4 as its threat window. Treat these as author claims, not measurements -- the repo's own goldfish and Forge simulator are the instruments that would settle it.

known_failure_modes: Artifact-and-ability stax. LearnCEDH names 'Vulnerability to Stax' with Collector Ouphe and Null Rod as the examples: one card turns off Basalt Monolith, Sol Ring and every rock simultaneously. Note the pilot already owns Collector Ouphe -- in a Kinnan deck it is a card that beats him.

Board wipes. The primer names 'Reliance on Nonland Mana Sources': with 27 lands and the mana on creatures, a sweeper is a Time Walk and a mana wipe at once, and there is no land base underneath to rebuild from.

Removal aimed at the commander. Felipe Torres: 'This deck depends a lot on the commander to generate value, and too much focus to deal with Kinnan ends up delaying the game plan a lot.' Kinnan is a two-mana 2/2 with no protection printed on him, and commander tax compounds each time.
Graveyard hate, per LearnCEDH's listed weaknesses, disrupting combo lines.
No black tutors: the deck cannot reliably find its missing half, so it wins when it draws well and durdles when it does not (Sasser).
contested: Thassa's Oracle. TheGamer's guide calls it 'the main win condition'; Drake Sasser writes that the deck 'passes on Thassa's Oracle despite being blue'. The mechanical reason they can both be reporting honestly: Simic has no Demonic Consultation or Tainted Pact, so Oracle only closes AFTER Thrasios has already drawn the library -- a sealing card, not a combo. The pilot owns Thassa's Oracle; he owns Demonic Consultation too, but it is mono-black and out of identity.

Land count. EDHREC's average Kinnan deck is 27 lands; A.L. Walser's mid-power build runs 33; TheGamer's cEDH guide claims 37, which is out of line with the other two and with a deck whose mana lives on nonland permanents. The 27 is a fleet average over 20,837 decks and is the figure I would trust; the 37 is one author's assertion.

Whether the three-card Freed from the Real lines fall under WotC's bracket-3 prohibition. The rule bans 'intentional early-game two-card infinite combos'; Kinnan + dork + Aura is literally three cards, but one of them is in the command zone, and Draftsim's writer describes the Basalt line as 'a one-piece combo since the other is in the command zone'. Not settled by any source I fetched. Moot for a bracket-4 build, which has no restrictions either way.

gaps: tappedout.net/mtg-decks/cedh-primer-kinnan-combo-prodigy/ returned HTTP 403 and moxfield.com/decks/FqFBbW1z80WWlmxZ0zJBrg/primer returned HTTP 403. I therefore have NO decklist-level counts from a primary competitive list -- no exact counterspell count, no exact dork/rock split for a bracket-4-or-5 build. Every count here is either an EDHREC aggregate or one article's list.

Ownership was checked card by card against the 931-name collection and is recorded in the 'ownership' key: 32 of the 110 cards named in this artifact are owned. Every one of the 110 was verified against data/cards.csv as Commander-legal and inside Kinnan's GU colour identity.

EDHREC's own cEDH figures disagree with themselves across two pages: the commander JSON reports a cEDH theme tag on 1,123 decks, while /commanders/kinnan-bonder-prodigy/cedh reported 4,198 decks 'with user-set cEDH brackets'. That fetch also returned composition figures it flagged as estimates, so I discarded its percentages entirely and used the main and Optimized pages instead. Which population the 4,198 describes is unresolved.

No source gives a MEASURED win-turn distribution for Kinnan. Every speed number here is an author assertion. The repo's goldfish and the Forge simulator against data/opponents/ are the instruments that would settle it, and should be run before the pilot buys on the strength of 'turn 3'.

I could not find a source discussing Kinnan specifically against a bracket-4 POD of fair decks -- how the deck plays when nobody at the table can counter the combo turn. Every primer assumes a cEDH table with free interaction on all four seats. This matters for the pilot's actual question and is the biggest hole in this recon.
The pilot does not own Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy himself; he is not in the 931-name collection.

No inclusion-rate source exists for 'what a bracket-4 pod finds acceptable', and there cannot be one. Whether this deck should be built is a decision for diagnose mode against the pod, not a fact recon can supply.
